streams.research_question: შეუძლია თუ არა site-specific წესებზე, მონაცემის სიახლესა და კალიბრაციის სტატუსზე დაფუძნებულმა operator-side სისტემამ ადრე მონიშნოს ოპერაციული გადახრები ისე, რომ არ ჩაანაცვლოს ლაბორატორიული ანალიზი ან უფლებამოსილი ოპერატორის გადაწყვეტილება?

Inventory official Georgian water-monitoring networks without combining unlike domains: NEA surface water, groundwater, marine water and the utility's raw-source/treated-network drinking-water testing are separate data streams.

Record only source-published network counts, monitoring frequency statements, parameter classes, laboratory accreditation claims and whether sample-level records/data dictionaries are publicly accessible; do not infer station-level frequency from a general news statement.

Before any ingestion, require an authorized data dictionary covering station ID/coordinates, sample timestamp, water matrix, analyte, result, units, method, LOD/LOQ, lab, accreditation, QA/QC flags, applicable standard, approved site Water Safety Plan limit, publication delay and revision history.

Evaluate any future sensor/lab pairing in shadow mode with preregistered detection delay, sensitivity, positive predictive value, false alerts per station-month, calibration drift and data completeness; require human and laboratory confirmation before operational action.

Review the 2025 Government of Georgia submission to the UNECE/WHO Protocol on Water and Health: keep NEA groundwater/surface-water monitoring separate from Food Safety Agency drinking-water compliance.

Inventory reported 2024 groundwater monitoring (72 points, 394 laboratory samples) and 2024 surface-water monitoring (331 points on 137 water bodies); preserve the report's aggregate/process evidence boundary.

Review the official 2026-11-26 NEA announcement of the 2021-2025 groundwater report and nitrate-risk field methodology; do not ingest the linked RAR archive until contents, schema and reuse terms are inspected.
Classify WIS C10/C11 as historical annual aggregates (2004-2018) and Hydromet's water-quality-points map/table as an unverified station-registry lead.
Treat 2024 E. coli non-compliance (40.3% source-reported) as a drinking-water sample statistic with missing denominator in the published table, not as population exposure.

Preserve countervailing source evidence: the UNECE/WHO government submission describes groundwater used as a drinking-water source as generally good quality, while noting isolated microbiological exceedances; do not infer a national groundwater crisis from the separate potable-network E. coli sample statistic.

Preserve the UNECE/WHO report's two E. coli reporting frames separately: narrative 2021-2022/2023/2024 and table baseline 2005/previous cycle 2019/current 2024; do not construct a continuous trend until definitions and denominators are reconciled.

Review Government of Georgia Resolution No.424 and NEA implementation notice; distinguish post-2026 wells >20 m from pre-existing and household wells, and treat the register as a prospective administrative metadata source rather than a sample-level monitoring feed.

Inspect the official MEPA GIS catalogue for groundwater station-layer metadata and distinguish a public/free catalogue classification from verified payload, download/API access, coordinate precision and reuse licence.
Keep the spatial station registry separate from sample-level analytical observations; require different adapters and schemas for station metadata, groundwater results and potable-network compliance.
Use Article 32 of Georgia's Law on Water Resources Management to distinguish NEA environmental-water monitoring data access from National Food Safety Agency drinking-water quality control.
Resolve the direct RAR archive URL linked by NEA's 2026-11-26 announcement; record the retrieval failure as an execution-environment limitation and do not infer archive contents or licence.

Keep NEA's 2025-09-18 disclosure of 72 groundwater points distinct from the 2025 annual report's 74 laboratory-sampling points, 73 listed-parameter points and 124 source-reported combined monitoring points; do not infer network growth, unique-site counts or overlap without a station/sample dictionary.
Translate the NEA source term “საკონტროლო ჭა” as “control well”; do not render it as “household well”.

On 2026-11-27, re-opened the official NEA announcement for the 2021–2025 groundwater report; the linked RAR was served as application/octet-stream and could not be inspected by the available web reader, while container-side DNS resolution also failed. Do not infer archive contents, data granularity or reuse terms.

Treat WRP 2025 WP22443 as self-reported harm only; preserve the publisher's code-1 plus code-3 rounded-sum definition and keep it separate from measured contamination, compliance and clinical outcomes.

Any independent reproduction must pin the exact WRP Parquet commit/blob, use PROJWT for pooled estimates, retain DK/refused in the stated denominator, and store only aggregate results and source hashes.
Cross-check the WHO 2026-11-19 drinking-water fact sheet while preserving separate reference years for faecal contamination (2022), safely managed coverage (2024) and annual mortality estimates.
Record the NFA 2025 violations workbook as metadata-only until authorized retrieval; inspect any payload in a controlled private workspace and do not estimate prevalence from a violations-only file.
Record the NFA 2026-08-12 Zugdidi drinking-water/lemonade facility inspection as a municipality-level regulatory-control event, explicitly separate from laboratory sample results and prevalence.

Compare the NFA 2026 planned drinking-water sampling allocation with actual collection/completion data only when published; preserve distributed-network, bottled-water and food/water investigation matrices as separate denominators.

WHO 2026 comparator cross-check: nitrate 50 mg/L as nitrate ion, nitrite 3 mg/L as nitrite ion, combined ratio <=1; fact sheet assessment date 2016. Treat as drinking-water guidance only, not Georgian law or an automatic raw-groundwater threshold.

Map Decree №58/2014 operational controls by supply mode: consumer tap, tank/cistern outlet, bottled filling/retail, and food-production water points; record supplier monitoring/response duties, emergency enhancement, repeat-sample triggers, routine analytes and accredited-lab requirement. Do not apply drinking-water compliance rules automatically to raw groundwater; legal transition after 2027-09-01 needs review.

Minimum annual sample counts are source-type and population-dependent under Article 3(2)/Table 7; process checks for residual chlorine/ozone and other reagents have separate hourly/per-shift frequencies. These are legal minimums, not observed sample counts.

Review Government Decree №447/2026: distinguish environmental water-resource monitoring from potable-water compliance; record NEA risk-based representative network, standard-format, public-access and data-quality duties.
Record Decree №447's observational, operational and investigative monitoring modes separately; do not infer every station or analyte is sampled monthly/quarterly from the operational-mode clause.
Preserve the EEA C11 nitrate reporting-basis distinction: rivers/lakes use mg NO3-N/L, while groundwater uses mg NO3/L.
Use an explicit Decimal-based NO3 to NO3-N conversion with the WHO-published rounded factor 0.226; retain original value, basis and water matrix.
Never use a rounded unit conversion as the sole basis for legal pass/fail classification near a threshold; compare each matrix against its applicable source-native standard.

Use the WHO Guidelines for drinking-water quality, fourth edition with the third addendum (17 June 2026), as the current international health-based comparator: nitrate 50 mg/L as NO3-, nitrite 3 mg/L as NO2-, combined ratio sum(C/GV) <=1, and 1 mg/L NO3- = 0.226 mg/L NO3-N.

Keep WHO health-based guideline values separate from Georgian legal requirements under Government Decree №58/2014; the Georgian nitrite value recorded in the decree is 0.2 mg/L as NO2-, not the WHO 3 mg/L comparator.

Calculate a combined nitrate/nitrite ratio only from paired measurements with the same sample identifier, water matrix, sampling point, collection time and compatible reporting bases; do not infer a ratio from separate aggregates.

Run 43: inspect the primary Matsne HTML for Decree №447/2026 and separately inspect Legali.ge's secondary annex transcription; preserve Annex-specific groundwater frequencies and nitrate/low-flow sampling methods as SECONDARY_TRANSCRIPTION_ONLY until the official DOCX is retrieved, SHA-256 verified and compared.

Keep Decree №447 main-text duties (FACT) separate from Annex-specific rows reproduced by a secondary legal mirror (SECONDARY_TRANSCRIPTION_ONLY); do not operationalize the latter before primary-attachment verification.

Run 43: re-open NEA's 2026-11-26 official announcement and record its stated report scope (2021–2025 groundwater quantitative/qualitative characteristics, automatic monitoring, historical-data digitization and network development) separately from the procurement contract's PDF/CD deliverables; the announcement is not sample-level data and the contract is not an acceptance act.

Run 45: review the official Matsne HTML of Government Decree №447 (2026-09-15), Articles 3–7, and cross-check the consolidated Water Resources Management Law (2026-09-16) Articles 31, 37 and 42. Separate state water-body monitoring from drinking-water consumer control; record matrix-specific and programme-specific requirements.

Run 45: pin the annual 1 December plan-submission deadline as upcoming on 2026-11-28; do not infer submission status before the deadline. Record the 2028-01-01 biota/sediment start date only for substances requiring those matrices.

Run 45 follow-up: cross-check Law Article 37(2)(b)(c)-(e); add the 2027-09-01 surface/groundwater nitrate-vulnerable-zone identification and good-agricultural-practice/action-plan milestone as a separate future requirement, not a completed finding.

Run 46: explicitly link the official 2021–2025 groundwater RAR payload to its NEA announcement page in the source-access inventory. Preserve the linked-but-not-extracted status; do not infer archive contents, sample-level data availability or reuse permission.

Run 47: primary-source review of Decree №424 Articles 2, 5 and 6 plus the annex; encode scope, deadlines, sampling states and privacy-sensitive field categories in a closed JSON Schema; synthetic tests only, no state-register records or real coordinates.

Run 49: compare the WHO 2026 consolidated nitrate/nitrite chemical fact sheet (printed pp. 466–472; assessment date 2016) with Georgian Decree №58/2014 Article 1, Table 4 and Article 2(21); preserve separate WHO-guidance and Georgian-legal regimes.

Run 50: track the Decree №447 Article 3(2)(a) deadline as submission to the Minister for approval, not a public-release deadline; without verified submission evidence after the due date, retain status as unverified and do not infer non-compliance.

Run 49: implement a Decimal-based nitrite reporting-basis conversion and a WHO-only combined-ratio helper that requires native ion bases, one pseudonymous sample ID, one timezone-aware timestamp and the drinking_water matrix; reject raw groundwater and cross-sample inputs.
Run 49: validate a closed legal/unit crosswalk and synthetic tests only; no sample-level Georgian results or operational alerts are generated.

Run 52: implement a metadata-only groundwater quantitative-status readiness gate from official Decree №447 Article 7(1)-(2); use hydrogeological-unit scope before groundwater-body designation and require caller-attested authority confirmation plus abstraction-data basis before assessment prerequisites are marked met.

Run 52: record Annex 2 groundwater frequencies and low-flow nitrate sampling only as SECONDARY_TRANSCRIPTION_ONLY from Legali.ge; the official 46,049-byte Matsne DOCX was not retrieved or hashed, so no Annex-derived production schedule is encoded.

Crosswalk historical NEAP-4 activity 5.1.8 against the later Law No.1766-Vმს-XIმპ Article 37(2)(b)(e); compare responsible actor, deadline, statutory basis, scope and formal deliverable without assuming equivalence.

Keep agency announcement, report-prepared status, final map, approval instrument and legal-compliance determination as separate evidence states; prototype only metadata coverage and require independent legal review.
Use the primary procurement contract as an alternate access/provenance route; distinguish contractual deliverables and due date from actual delivery, acceptance, publication and reuse permission.

Run 54: review the 2026 New Zealand national retrospective cohort on nitrate and preterm birth; preserve exposure in mg/L NO3-N and record reported odds ratios as source-reported facts, not independently reproduced results.

Run 54: compare the corrected Danish expert report (2026-01-07), WHO 2026 consolidated guideline (nitrate fact-sheet assessment 2016), and Georgia Decree №58/2014; keep expert recommendation, international guidance and national regulatory text in separate provenance classes.

Run 54: implement a typed nitrate benchmark provenance guard; it rejects cross-matrix and cross-basis comparisons, rejects epidemiological studies as thresholds, and never returns legal-compliance or potability decisions.

Separate source-link resolution, byte retrieval, checksum verification, document-content review and legal interpretation as distinct evidence stages; a failed client fetch is not evidence of source-server outage.
Track the 2026-12-01 annual-plan submission duty separately from approval and public release; absence of a public file does not prove non-submission.

Run 56: map Government Decree No.447 Articles 3-7 into a metadata-only annual-plan evidence intake; keep plan retrieval, ministerial submission, approval, annex inspection and monitoring execution as separate states.

streams.research_question: შეუძლია თუ არა ოფიციალური გაფრთხილებისგან დამოუკიდებელ, privacy-preserving action-readiness ფენას გააუმჯობესოს კონკრეტულ მაღალი რისკის თემებში გაფრთხილების გაგება, მიღება და feasible protective action ისე, რომ არ შექმნას დუბლირებული ოფიციალური გაფრთხილება?
streams.human_benefit: საფრთხის წინასწარი ცოდნის რეალურ, დროულ და ადამიანზე მორგებულ დამცავ მოქმედებად გარდაქმნა; შესაძლო სარგებელი მოიცავს სიცოცხლის, ჯანმრთელობისა და ქონების დაცვას.
streams.hypothesis: თუ ოფიციალური გაფრთხილება დაკავშირებულია ლოკალურ რისკთან, წინასწარ შეთანხმებულ მოქმედების playbook-თან, პასუხისმგებელ ორგანიზაციასთან, ხელმისაწვდომ საკომუნიკაციო არხთან და acknowledgement/action audit-თან, შეიძლება შემცირდეს გაფრთხილებიდან მოქმედებამდე დრო და გაიზარდოს რეაგირების დაფარვა.

Run 47: preserve WRP survey context (population-weighted, retrospective, self-reported) as a separate evidence lane from event-level operational aggregates; do not combine denominators or interpret cross-sectional subgroup gradients causally.

UNDRR COP31's 4/5 warning-receipt and 1/3 unable-to-act statement has no underlying method in the cited page and must not be treated as a calibrated global baseline.
Warning receipt, timely receipt, comprehension, feasibility, action and avoided loss are distinct stages; combining marginal rates or inferring causal impact would be invalid.

A credential-bearing or signed source URL stored in a public metadata record could disclose access tokens; the current URL screening is heuristic and cannot detect every secret embedded in every possible URL representation.

The reported nearly sixfold lower disaster mortality in countries with comprehensive versus limited/moderate MHEWS is a cross-country association; confounding and ecological inference prevent causal attribution to warning systems alone.
URL structural validation is not publisher authentication, signature validation, DNS/SSRF protection, or evidence that a warning was delivered, understood or acted upon.
Decree №440 establishes preliminary risk assessment duties, not operational alert issuance/delivery or protective-action performance.
Future methodology and first national assessment deadlines are not evidence that maps or identified risk areas already exist.
Mudflow and glacial-lake-outburst processes are conditional considerations where needed, not asserted as mandatory for every basin.

NEA's 2026-11-25 notice describes plan preparation/consultation, while GEO Outlook's secondary implementer page says plans were developed for seven basins and contains an inconsistent 'for 4 river basins' phrase. Do not infer formal approval, adoption, publication or implementation without signed primary plan documents.

The 2025, April 2026 and November 2026 Agency notices describe different programme stages; do not collapse risk-assessment validation, plan drafting, consultation, formal approval, publication and operational implementation into one completion status.
Channel-count and household-plan/agency gradients are cross-sectional self-reported associations; confounding by hazard severity, exposure and resources prevents causal interpretation.
Endpoint delivery confirmations are not people; survey receipt, comprehension, feasibility and action are different denominators and must not be collapsed into one success score.
The minimum-cell-size floor of 10 is a NOEMA release-policy floor, not a legal safe harbour; higher suppression or coarser geography may be required after threat modelling.
The 298 hydrometeorological station/watchpoint figure is a 2026 year-end target reported on 14 July, not an observed November 2026 installed/operational count.
Hydrometeorological stations, landslide monitoring bodies and server-platform integrations are different units and cannot be combined into one coverage percentage.
